Pussyfooting around Putin

By: Marion Edmunds | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Tonight on Carte Blanche we examine why the South African government is pussy-footing around Putin and why it may be dangerous for the country

Unique Selling Point:
This is the hot topic of the moment which has engaged two government ministries, and both wings of the Presidency plus numerous civil society bodies and commentators - and the brouhaha around Putin's potential visit throws South Africa drift into isolationism into sharp focus.

Summary:
The ANC’s political allegiance to its Cold War friend, Russia, is causing a political rumpus as a potential visit to South Africa by Russian President Vladimir Putin forces the South African government to make choices, including whether or not it leaves the International Criminal Court, which may reset its already damaged global reputation for the worse.

The ICC has issued a warrant of arrest for Putin for the kidnapping of thousands of Ukrainian children during the conflict between the neighbours. As South Africa is a signatory to the Rome Statute which underpins the ICC, it would be obliged to arrest Putin if he comes to South Africa. Putin was expected to arrive for the BRICS summit in August this year along with leaders of the countries aligned with South Africa in this economic block – Brazil, India and China.

The Premier of the Western Cape, Alan Winde, says he will get his unarmed LEAP officers to arrest Putin if strays into the Western Cape, a province under the political control of the opposition. While this throws up the spectacle of the absurd – unarmed para-police officials arresting one of the world’s militaristic strong men – it has set the cat further among the pigeons, sending the government into a legal huddle as it tries to work out what to do. Already the issue is being passed from ministry to ministry as the legal ramifications of a potential Putin visit are examined, the tension between the political party, the ANC, the government and the interests of the economy and South Africa’s citizens are weighed up, not to mention South Africa’s constitutional commitment to a human rights based foreign policy.

This political hot potato is just one more milestone in South Africa’s slow drift to isolationism, which has been compounded by greyl-isting, industrial-scale corruption, poor governance, loss of investor confidence and a clumsy foreign policy which appears to be biased ideologically to the allies of the ANC, rather than drawn from a strategic positioning of South Africa to get the maximum benefit from trade and political opportunities from the Global North.

We look at the event, the discussions around it and the consequences of pussy-footing around Putin, in the context of this dangerous drift, in which so much of the country’s moral and financial capital could be squandered.

Script:


(VO) ON THE 25TH OF APRIL, THE ANC SECRETARY GENERAL FIKILE MBALULA DROPPED A BOMB SHELL - SOUTH AFRICA WOULD LEAVE ONE OF THE MOST IMPORTANT GLOBAL INSTITUTIONS SET UP TO PREVENT CRIMES AGAINST HUMANITY.

Fikile Mbalula
Secretary-General of the ANC
ICC withdrawal - it was a decision that was taken long time ago by the ANC.

(VO) A FEW HOURS LATER, PRESIDENT CYRIL RAMAPHOSA FOLLOWED IT UP WITH A CONFIRMATION.

CYRIL RAMAPHOSA: Yes, the governing party the African National Congress has taken that decision, that it is prudent that South Africa should pull out of the ICC…

(VO)BUT DRAMATICALLY THE ANNOUNCEMENT WAS LATER CORRECTED BY HIS OWN OFFICE - SOUTH AFRICA WOULD IN FACT NOT FORSAKE THE ICC.

Nicole Fritz
Director: Helen Suzman Foundation
I hope whoever briefed, the President offered him fulsome apologies, because obviously, he got an erroneous briefing. And unfortunately, it doesn't want to be making that type of error when so much of the world's media is focused on South Africa.

(VO)NICOLE FRITZ IS AS AN EXPERT IN INTERNATIONAL CRIMINAL LAW…

(VO)SHE CAN EXPLAIN THE TECHNICAL DETAIL BEHIND THE GLOBAL POLITICS OF THE ICC, AS WELL AS THE CRITICISM AGAINST IT…

Nicole Fritz
Director: Helen Suzman Foundation
It’s the first global court that looks to try individuals for atrocity crimes, genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes. And so it differs from other global courts, which generally adjudicate matters between states, countries. Here it is actual individuals who face accountability for their involvement in these atrocity crimes.

(VO) WEEKS EARLIER THE ICC HAD ISSUED A WARRANT OF ARREST FOR RUSSIAN PRESIDENT VLADIMIR PUTIN FOR THE ABDUCTION OF HUNDREDS OF UKRAINIAN CHILDREN DURING THE RUSSIAN OFFENSIVE IN UKRAINE.

JUDGE PITOR HOFMANSKI: This is an important moment in the process of justice before the ICC. …. The judges issued arrest warrants, their execution depends on international cooperation.

(VO) NOW LIKE OTHER WAR CRIMINALS IDENTIFIED BY THE ICC, THE RUSSIAN HEAD OF STATE IS A WANTED MAN. BUT VLADIMIR PUTIN WAS SCHEDULED TO TRAVEL TO DURBAN IN AUGUST TO ATTEND A BRICS SUMMIT WITH LEADERS OF REGIONAL TRADE PARTNERS, BRAZIL, INDIA, CHINA AND SOUTH AFRICA.

Masa Kekana - Piece to camera:
As things stand now, the South African government would be obliged to arrest Mr Putin shoudl he put foot on South African soil. But that’s a bit awkward now because the governing ANC and Russia are good friends.

MASA: So South Africa is in a very difficult position here?

Nicole Fritz
Director: Helen Suzman Foundation
South Africa is in a very difficult position here, South Africa is and there's no two ways about it is a very complicated diplomatic dilemma.

(VO)THE UKRAINE AMBASSADOR, LIUBOV ABRAVITOVA, KNOWS ALL ABOUT DIPLOMATIC DILEMMAS. SHE DEALS WITH SOUTH AFRICA’S DECLARED POSITION OF NEUTRALITY IN A WAR WHICH FROM HER PERSPECTIVE IS AN INVASION OF HER HOMELAND.

Liubov Abravitova
Ukraine Ambassador in South Africa
As of today, officially confirmed, that 19,390 children are still in the captivity of Russia in Russian Federation. We don't know the real numbers, and we anticipate that they're much higher….
Now, this is the matter of time and the matter of the desire of every country who is the signatory to the Rome Statute to fulfil its obligation under this or not.

(VO)THE DAY AFTER THE ICC U-TURN, RAMAPHOSA’S POLITICAL OPPONENTS SENT OFF A SALVO OF THEIR OWN. IT CAME FROM MAJESTIC LEEUWENHOF, THE SEAT OF THE WESTERN CAPE PREMIER.

Masa Kekana - Piece to camera:
On the 27th of April, Freedom Day, Western Province Premier Alan Winde, put out a press statement that touched a raw nerve.

ALAN WINDE FROM TWITTER:
There’s no flipflopping here in the Western Cape, if Vladimir Putin comes here, our law enforcement officers will arrest him and send him to the courts! (Applause)

Alan Winde
Western Cape Premier
I can think of nothing worse than trainloads of children being shipped out of the home country into Russia as part of a lever of trying to win a war. I mean, that is an absolute atrocity. … And I said, Well, in this province, it will be clear, we will abide by that international criminal court ruling. And of course, if that happens in the Western Cape, if Putin comes here, then I will make sure that we go through our processes to have him arrested.

(VO) THE MINISTER IN THE PRESIDENCY FIRED BACK BY GUARANTEEING PUTIN A SPECIAL GUARD.

Minister in the Presidency Khumbudzo Ntshavheni:
I don’t know how Premier Winde who does not even have even policing functions, will then get through our presidential protection service, and I am sure you have seen the capacity and capability of our Presidential protection service. So Premier Winde can dream about whatever….

Masa Kekana Question: Would you say it was you trying to show leadership?

Alan Winde
Western Cape Premier
We need to be much stronger in South Africa about how we position our country, we're a democracy. We're a player in the world. Thinking back to Freedom Day, what really bothered me is 29 years ago, the whole world looked at us as this miracle. … there were hopes and there were dreams, and 29 years later, we can't even keep the lights on.

Masa Kekana - Piece to camera:
Loadshedding, corruption, greylisting, coalition drama and now add to the mix - whether Russian President Vladimir Putin should visit this country.
Is South Africa trashing it’s own brand?

Zukile Majova
Political Editor of Scrolla.Africa
Russia is an aggressor. You can’t ignore that. There’s no way you can vote for what is going on in the Ukraine.

(VO) ZUKILE MAJOVA IS THE POLITICAL EDITOR FOR THIS START-UP MOBILE NEWS PLATFORM SCROLLA.AFRICA. IT PUBLISHES IN ENGLISH, ZULU AND AFRIKAANS. HE HAS HIS EAR TO THE GROUND FOR POLITICAL STORIES.

ZUKILE MAJOVA, Political Editor of Scrolla.Africa
If you look at Nelson Mandela, he had a global respect. He had that
stature. President Thabo Mbeki had passion about African Renaissance and African solutions to African problems. …. Things are changing…..We've not been invited to Japan, for the for the next G7. Things are changing. (Maybe put in first Things are changing)

(VO) MAJOVA BELIEVES THAT THIS BLUNDER IS TAINTING THE REPUTATION OF PRESIDENT CYRIL RAMAPHOSA.

ZUKILE MAJOVA, Political Editor of Scrolla.Africa
If you look in the last elections, it was not really the ANC that won the election. It was Ramaphosa himself that won the election for the ANC. What is about to happen now to the ANC? It's people now losing a bit of faith, not on the ANC. They've lost faith in the ANC for a long time now, people next year are going to be losing faith in Ramaphosa because they kept the ANC in power based on their understanding of this man.

(VO) BUT DIPLOMACY IS NOT THE ONLY STUMBLING BLOCK.

ONCE THE DARLING OF THE EMERGING MARKETS, SOUTH AFRICA HAS RECENTLY BEEN GREYLISTED.
THAT SERVES AS A GLOBAL ALARM BELL TO WARN THAT INVESTMENT HERE MAY BE AT RISK.
IT COMES AFTER A SPECTACULAR BREAKDOWN OF FINANCIAL CONTROLS ACROSS THE ECONOMY.

ECONOMIST, DR IRAJ ABEDIAN, HAS BEEN AN OUTSPOKEN OBSERVER OF SOUTH AFRICAN CAPITAL FOR DECADES.

Iraj Abedian, CE of Pan-African Capital Holdings and Research
These are not also irrelevant theoretical issues, they affect the lives and the welfare of the working class and every other citizen. I'm focusing on working class because obviously South Africa has got a poverty issue, unemployment issue, inequality issue. So a cabinet that sits there and says, are no we are at the risk of greylisting. We've been, we've been diagnosed by the early signs of cancer, but let's smoke in any case, ignore it. That's poor leadership for me.

(VO) IN THE MEANTIME THERE IS NO EASY SOLUTION TO THE PUTIN PROBLEM - IT’S YET ANOTHER LITMUS TEST OF THE CREDIBILITY OF SOUTH AFRICAN LEADERS, A YEAR BEFORE A CRITICAL ELECTION.

Masa Kekana - Piece to camera:
Ministries have been scrambling for legal opinion to try and find a work around, and one of these may play out in Parliament, as the ruling party may try to tweak the law to among other things, give visiting heads of state immunity from arrest.

(VO) CHANGING THE LAW TO GIVE THE RUSSIAN PRESIDENT BREATHING SPACE IN POST-APARTHEID SOUTH AFRICA SEEMS LIKE A DIFFICULT COMPROMISE.

Nicole Fritz
Director: Helen Suzman Foundation
We were a champion of the ICC at at its inception. And I think our involvement in the ICC, South Africa, the involvement of a democratic South Africa, was very much kind of prompted and motivated by South Africa's experience of apartheid and the fact that they weren't laws on the books that allowed often for prosecutions of the crime of apartheid.

WILL PUTIN COME TO SOUTH AFRICA IN AUGUST?
UNTIL THE LAST MINUTE, THE PUBLIC MAY WELL BE KEPT GUESSING…



PUTIN PROMOS:
2X 21 SECONDERS

(VO)
A DIPLOMATIC BLUNDER…
OVER A WANTED MAN…..

ALAN WINDE FROM TWITTER:
There’s no flipflopping here in the Western Cape, if Vladimir Putin comes here, our law enforcement officers will arrest him and send him to the courts! (Applause)

Nicole Fritz
Director: Helen Suzman Foundation
…. it is a very complicated diplomatic dilemma.

(VO)
FRIEND OR FOE - VLADIMIR PUTIN MAY VISIT SOUTH AFRICA…
Zukile Majova
Political Editor of Scrolla.Africa
Russia is an aggressor. You can’t ignore that.

(VO) FIGHT OR FLIGHT - WHO WILL BLINK FIRST…
Alan Winde
Western Cape Premier
…if Putin comes here, then I will make sure that we go through our processes to have him arrested.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Tonight on Carte Blanche we examine why the South African government is pussy-footing around Putin and why it may be dangerous for the country
metadata.Unique Selling Point: This is the hot topic of the moment which has engaged two government ministries, and both wings of the Presidency plus numerous civil society bodies and commentators - and the brouhaha around Putin's potential visit throws South Africa drift into isolationism into sharp focus.
metadata.Summary: The ANC’s political allegiance to its Cold War friend, Russia, is causing a political rumpus as a potential visit to South Africa by Russian President Vladimir Putin forces the South African government to make choices, including whether or not it leaves the International Criminal Court, which may reset its already damaged global reputation for the worse. The ICC has issued a warrant of arrest for Putin for the kidnapping of thousands of Ukrainian children during the conflict between the neighbours. As South Africa is a signatory to the Rome Statute which underpins the ICC, it would be obliged to arrest Putin if he comes to South Africa. Putin was expected to arrive for the BRICS summit in August this year along with leaders of the countries aligned with South Africa in this economic block – Brazil, India and China. The Premier of the Western Cape, Alan Winde, says he will get his unarmed LEAP officers to arrest Putin if strays into the Western Cape, a province under the political control of the opposition. While this throws up the spectacle of the absurd – unarmed para-police officials arresting one of the world’s militaristic strong men – it has set the cat further among the pigeons, sending the government into a legal huddle as it tries to work out what to do. Already the issue is being passed from ministry to ministry as the legal ramifications of a potential Putin visit are examined, the tension between the political party, the ANC, the government and the interests of the economy and South Africa’s citizens are weighed up, not to mention South Africa’s constitutional commitment to a human rights based foreign policy. This political hot potato is just one more milestone in South Africa’s slow drift to isolationism, which has been compounded by greyl-isting, industrial-scale corruption, poor governance, loss of investor confidence and a clumsy foreign policy which appears to be biased ideologically to the allies of the ANC, rather than drawn from a strategic positioning of South Africa to get the maximum benefit from trade and political opportunities from the Global North. We look at the event, the discussions around it and the consequences of pussy-footing around Putin, in the context of this dangerous drift, in which so much of the country’s moral and financial capital could be squandered.
